sections.body: Explanation.–The words “lawful guardian” in this clause include any person lawfully entrusted with the care or custody of such child or other person

sections.heading: Exceptions and provisos
sections.body:
Exception.—This clause does not extend to the act of any person who in good faith believes himself to be the father of an illegitimate child, or who in good faith believes himself to be entitled to the lawful custody of such child, unless such act is committed for an immoral or unlawful purpose
(2) Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 137 (Kidnapping) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 137 (Kidnapping), Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Kidnapping is of two kinds: kidnapping from India, and kidnapping from lawful guardianship–
   (2) (a) whoever conveys any person beyond the limits of India without the consent of that person, or of some person legally authorised to consent on behalf of that person, is said to kidnap that person from India;
   (3) (b) whoever takes or entices any child or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian of such child or person of unsound mind, without the consent of such guardian, is said to kidnap such child or person from lawful guardianship
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 137 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 137 (Kidnapping)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 137 deals with Kidnapping. It sits in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Kidnapping: from India, or from lawful guardianship. Taking or enticing a child (male under 18, female under 18) out of the keeping of the lawful guardian without consent. The minor’s consent is irrelevant.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 137 is the rule on “Kidnapping”. The section provides that (1) Kidnapping is of two kinds: kidnapping from India, and kidnapping from lawful guardianship–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. (1) Kidnapping is of two kinds: kidnapping from India, and kidnapping from lawful guardianship–
2. (a) whoever conveys any person beyond the limits of India without the consent of that person, or of some person legally authorised to consent on behalf of that person, is said to kidnap that person from India;
3. (b) whoever takes or entices any child or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian of such child or person of unsound mind, without the consent of such guardian, is said to kidnap such child or person from lawful guardianship

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Explanations. Explanation.–The words “lawful guardian” in this clause include any person lawfully entrusted with the care or custody of such child or other person An explanation is not optional commentary. It is part of the section and must appear in an authoritative brief.

Exceptions / provisos. Exception.—This clause does not extend to the act of any person who in good faith believes himself to be the father of an illegitimate child, or who in good faith believes himself to be entitled to the lawful custody of such child, unless such act is committed for an immoral or unlawful purpose

(2) Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fin… State the exception and then say whether it is attracted on the facts.

Connected sections. Read with BNS s. 138, BNS s. 140. A preliminary brief mentions the neighbour; comprehensive submissions explain the exact distinction.

Conclusion. BNS s. 137 is the complete current-law heading for Kidnapping. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

learningObjectives: Master the definition of kidnapping and its two statutory classifications under BNS s. 137.
Analyze Kidnapping from India under sub-section (1)(a) and Kidnapping from Lawful Guardianship under sub-section (1)(b).
Examine the age thresholds under sub-section (1)(b): male under sixteen years, female under eighteen years, or person of unsound mind.
Understand the statutory Exception protecting putative fathers acting in good faith.
Examine the baseline punishment of imprisonment up to seven years and fine under sub-section (2).
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 137 consolidates the law of kidnapping: sub-section (1) provides that kidnapping is of two kinds: (a) kidnapping from India (conveying any person beyond the limits of India without consent); and (b) kidnapping from lawful guardianship (taking or enticing any child under sixteen years if male, under eighteen years if female, or person of unsound mind out of the keeping of the lawful guardian without consent); sub-section (2) punishes kidnapping with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Protects territorial sovereignty and parental custody by criminalizing the non-consensual removal of individuals beyond India's borders and the taking of minors from lawful guardianship.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 137 (consolidating IPC ss. 359, 360, 361, and 363).
Sub-section (1)(a): Kidnapping from India — conveying beyond limits of India without consent of person or authorized guardian.
Sub-section (1)(b): Kidnapping from lawful guardianship — taking or enticing minor (male under 16, female under 18) or person of unsound mind out of lawful guardianship without consent.
Sub-section (2): Punishment — imprisonment of either description up to seven years, and fine.
Explanation: 'Lawful guardian' includes any person lawfully entrusted with the care or custody of the minor.
Exception: Act of person who in good faith believes himself to be the father of an illegitimate child, or believes himself entitled to lawful custody, unless done for immoral or unlawful purpose.
essentialIngredients: For Kidnapping from India: A person was conveyed beyond the territorial limits of India without their consent (or guardian's consent).
For Kidnapping from Guardianship: The victim was a male under sixteen years, a female under eighteen years, or a person of unsound mind.
The victim was in the keeping of a lawful guardian.
The accused took or enticed the victim out of such keeping.
The taking or enticing was done WITHOUT the consent of the lawful guardian.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 137 consolidates the definition (former IPC 359, 360, 361) and general punishment (former IPC 363) of kidnapping into a single cohesive structure. Kidnapping from India is purely territorial, requiring conveyance across national borders without consent. Kidnapping from lawful guardianship is an offence primarily against parental and custodial rights. The law specifies distinct age limits: under sixteen years for males, and under eighteen years for females. The actus reus requires 'taking' (active physical removal) or 'enticing' (alluring or persuading through gifts, promises, or romance) the minor out of the guardian's custody. The consent of the minor is completely irrelevant in law; the only consent that matters is that of the lawful guardian. The statutory Exception shields a person who in good faith believes himself entitled to custody (such as the father of an illegitimate child), provided the custody is not sought for an immoral or unlawful purpose.
examples: Teaching example (Enticing a 17-year-old girl): An adult man persuades a seventeen-year-old girl to pack her bags and slip out of her parents' house at midnight to travel to another city with him. Even though the girl willingly agreed, the accused is guilty of kidnapping from lawful guardianship under s. 137(1)(b) because parental consent was absent.

Teaching example (Taking a child from school): A stranger picks up a seven-year-old boy from outside his primary school and takes him to another town without the parents' knowledge. This is kidnapping under s. 137(2).
distinctions: Kidnapping (s. 137) vs Abduction (s. 138): Kidnapping is committed only against minors (or out of India), requires no force or fraud, and minor's consent is void; Abduction applies to persons of ANY age and strictly requires force or deceit.
Kidnapping (s. 137) vs Section 140 (Kidnapping for ransom/murder): Section 137 is simple kidnapping (up to 7 years); Section 140 is aggravated kidnapping carrying death or life imprisonment.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who drove away with a 15-year-old boy after offering him money to run away from his parents' home is guilty of kidnapping, even though the boy begged to leave home.
Rule: Enticing a male under sixteen out of the keeping of a lawful guardian without the guardian's consent constitutes kidnapping under BNS s. 137, irrespective of the child's consent.
Application: The victim was 15 years old (under 16), in lawful custody, and removed without parental consent.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of kidnapping under BNS s. 137(2).

Two kinds: from India, and from lawful guardianship.
Age limits: male under 16, female under 18; minor's consent is legally void.
Punishable with imprisonment up to seven years and fine.
